lead: Spring Boot builds a web service you start with one command. It packs an embedded Tomcat inside your JAR, so you install no separate server. @RestController turns a Java method into a URL that answers JSON. Spring Data JPA turns a repository call into SQL against a real table. Teams use this stack for payment APIs, order services and mobile backends. Only a few universities teach it. You need servlet request and response and REST, JSON and databases (Unit 6).
prereq: You need: 4.7 Java Servlets, and Unit 6 REST, JSON and databases.

blocks.text: A Spring Boot project is a Maven project with a parent that fixes library versions. You add a starter, not a library: a starter is a bundle of dependencies tested together.

items: spring-boot-starter-web brings Spring MVC, Jackson for JSON, and embedded Tomcat.
spring-boot-starter-data-jpa brings JPA and Hibernate; the H2 or MySQL driver is added separately.

blocks.text: The class carrying @SpringBootApplication is three annotations in one: @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration and @ComponentScan. Its main method calls SpringApplication.run(App.class, args).

Auto-configuration reads application.properties. Set spring.datasource.url, spring.datasource.username and spring.datasource.password for the database. Add spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update so Hibernate creates or alters tables.
Embedded Tomcat starts inside the same Java process, by default on port 8080. mvn package builds one runnable JAR, and java -jar app.jar starts the whole service on any machine with a JVM.
@RestController marks a class whose methods return data, not page names. Spring MVC maps the URL to a method, then Jackson writes the returned object as JSON.
The mapping annotation fixes the HTTP method: @GetMapping reads, @PostMapping inserts, @PutMapping and @DeleteMapping handle the rest. A path such as /api/students/{id} holds a placeholder.

items: @PathVariable Long id reads {id} from the URL and converts it to Long.
@RequestBody Student s reads the JSON body and converts it to a Student.
ResponseEntity<Student> carries body and status together: ResponseEntity.status(201).body(saved).

blocks.text: A plain returned object gets status 200. Use ResponseEntity when the status must differ, for example 201 after an insert.

sections.h3: Spring Data JPA: an interface that writes SQL

blocks.text: JPA maps a class to a table. @Entity marks the class, @Id marks the primary key, and @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY) lets the database supply the next id. The class needs a public no-arg constructor, because Hibernate builds instances by reflection.

A repository is an interface, not a class: interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long>. The two type parameters are the entity and the id type. Spring writes the implementation at startup.

items: findById(1L) returns Optional<Student> and runs a SELECT by primary key.
save(s) runs INSERT when the id is null and UPDATE when it is set.

blocks.text: For learning use H2 in memory: jdbc:h2:mem:testdb. For a real service use MySQL: jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/college.

spec.aria: Controller, repository and Hibernate boxes lead to the SQL SELECT and the student table with rows 1 Anu 78 and 2 Ravi 65; replies 200 with Anu as JSON and 201 with Ravi as JSON.

examples.question: The table student has columns id, name and marks, and row (1, Anu, 78) exists. Write the entity, repository and controller for GET /api/students/1 and give the JSON. Then give the POST that adds Ravi with 65 marks, and its response.
steps: Entity Student: @Entity, @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY) Long id, String name, int marks, and a no-arg constructor. Hibernate maps it to table student.
Repository: interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long>. Spring generates the class; findById(1L) becomes SELECT * FROM student WHERE id = 1.
Controller: @RestController with @GetMapping("/{id}") and method Student one(@PathVariable Long id) { return repo.findById(id).orElseThrow(); }.
Jackson writes the returned object as {"id":1,"name":"Anu","marks":78}. The method returned normally, so the status is 200.

POST /api/students with body {"name":"Ravi","marks":65}: @RequestBody builds a Student, repo.save inserts the row, IDENTITY returns id 2, and ResponseEntity.status(201) sends 201 with {"id":2,"name":"Ravi","marks":65}.
examples.answer: GET /api/students/1 returns 200 with {"id":1,"name":"Anu","marks":78}; POST returns 201 with {"id":2,"name":"Ravi","marks":65}.

traps: An @Entity without @Id, or without a no-arg constructor, fails at startup; Hibernate also needs getters or field access, so pick one style.
JpaRepository is an interface. You never write new StudentRepository(); you inject it into the controller constructor.
Returning the entity leaks every column and can trigger lazy loading while Jackson writes JSON; a DTO is safer.
@Controller returns a view name, @RestController writes the body. Mixing them gives a rendered page or a 404, not JSON.
@PathVariable reads the URL, @RequestBody reads the JSON body. Swapping them gives a null field or a 400.

quiz.q: What does @RestController add to a class?
quiz.a: @Controller plus @ResponseBody, so return values are written as the response body instead of a view name.

quiz.q: Why does Spring Data JPA need only an interface for a repository?
quiz.a: Spring generates the implementing proxy at startup from JpaRepository's declared methods, so findById and save need no hand-written SQL.

quiz.q: The table already holds ids 1 and 2. A POST body is {"name":"Meera","marks":91}. Give the saved id and the response.
findById returns Optional<Student>. What happens by default when the id is missing and the method calls orElseThrow()?
quiz.a: It throws NoSuchElementException, which Spring maps to 500; a 404 needs an explicit exception handler.

quiz.q: Which embedded server does Spring Boot start by default, and on which port?

quiz.a: @PathVariable reads one value from the URL path; @RequestBody deserializes the whole JSON body into an object.

beyond: Not for the exam. Spring Boot is the default Java backend in Indian service companies, so the next steps are Spring Security with JWT for login tokens, Actuator for health and metrics endpoints, and Testcontainers for tests against a real MySQL. Spring Cloud adds service discovery and central configuration once one service becomes ten. Docker packaging and CI/CD pipelines follow. Search 'spring boot jpa crud example', 'spring boot actuator health' and 'testcontainers mysql junit'.
